newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nuclear waste convoy arrives at German dump.
newsitem.headline: Nuclear waste convoy arrives at German dump.

text.p: A controversial shipment of nuclear waste arrived on Wednesday in a convoy of trucks at its final destination -- Gorleben storage depot in northern Germany, amid huge protests by hundreds of activists.

The trucks carrying six 90-tonne containers of spent fuel rods arrived under heavy police protection in Germany's largest post-war security operation after thousands of protesters tried to disrupt its journey across the country from the south.

About 5,000 demonstrators set up blockades and in some place clashed with police along the 20-km (14-mile) route from a loading station in Dannenberg, where the waste arrived early on Tuesday, to Gorleben dump.
Thousands of police and border guards were posted in the area while heavy police cordons escorted the shipment to its final destination.
The operation will cost at least 66 million marks ($39 million) and surpass the 46 million marks spent on bringing a smaller shipment to Gorleben last year.

The waste from two German power stations and a French reprocessing plant was transported by train from the southern town of Walheim early on Monday and was unloaded onto flat-bed trucks in the northern town of Dannenberg on Tuesday.
